title: Go frontend: codecs, partiality, slice headers, pipelines, loop bounds

predictions.claim: The extracted layouts equal the frozen ones (enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1). (morph-l2/common/batch.BatchHeaderV0).Bytes and (...BatchHeaderV1).Bytes each have exactly two return paths: the cache path, cond [[">", len(b.EncodedBytes), 0]], returning a view of b.EncodedBytes (V1 tests its own EncodedBytes field, which shadows the embedded V0's), and the layout path, cond [["<=", len(b.EncodedBytes), 0]], returning a fresh buffer allocated at batch_header.go:216 / :244 of length and capacity 249 / 257. That buffer gives each encoder exactly one layout, exact, equal cell for cell to the frozen facts' layout under the field map of facts/morph_header.json types.Header (frozen field -> the Go field named first in its "go" text): cell 0 is ["const", 0] / ["const", 1], every other cell is byte k of a field of the receiver, reached through the embedded BatchHeaderV0 in V1 for every field except LastBlockNumber; no path panics. Prior evidence: results/M2/refinement/enc_go_v0.json and enc_go_v1.json (I16) sampled the frozen layouts against the real Bytes() with 0 disagreements; what is predicted is that the static extraction from SSA, which never reads the frozen facts, reproduces them exactly.

Decoder partiality equals ok_go on every length constant +-1. Probes (tests_m2/_i18.probes): every getter offset and offset + width of the frozen dec_go and every ok_go length (1, 9, 17, 25, 57, 89, 121, 153, 185, 217, 249, 257), each -1, 0, +1, plus 0, 1, 2 (36 lengths), byte 0 in 0, 1, 2, 3, 255, cap = len and len + 16 (352 probes). On every probe exactly one extracted path of each function holds; for validate (frozen ok_go), Hash and the 12 frozen dec_go getters (each mapped to the BatchHeaderBytes method its frozen code names: Version, BatchIndex, L1MessagePopped, TotalL1MessagePopped, DataHash, BlobCommitHash, PrevStateRoot, PostStateRoot, WithdrawalRoot, SequencerSetVerifyHash, ParentBatchHash, LastBlockNumber) that path returns a nil error iff frozen ok_go holds and the getter's frozen when holds (LastBlockNumber: version >= 1), except Version, which the frozen ok_go 'empty' rule names: nil iff length >= 1; otherwise a non-nil error; no holding path panics. Every frozen getter's extracted reads are exactly [(offset, width)] of the frozen getter. Prior evidence: results/M2/refinement/dec_go.json and ok_go.json (I16) sampled these on a boundary corpus; predicted here is the static, exact partiality.

BatchHeaderBytes in morph-l2/common/batch has exactly 14 decoders: the 12 frozen getters' methods, BlobVersionedHash and BlobHashesHash (both reading (57, 32)). On every I18-P2 probe BlobVersionedHash returns nil iff ok_go and byte 0 < 2, BlobHashesHash iff ok_go and byte 0 >= 2, and BlobCommitHash (it dispatches to one of the two on Version()) iff ok_go, never panicking.

There is no v2 encoder in the codec package (O2, recorded as an absence). validate is a tagged predicate, tag_index 0, accepting exactly (0, 249), (1, 257), (2, 257); the encoder matches are V0.Bytes for (0, 249), V1.Bytes for (1, 257) and, for (2, 257), only morph-l2/morph-deployer/morph-chain-ops/genesis.GenesisBatchHeader, so morph_batch's absences are exactly one: version 2 at length 257, elsewhere [GenesisBatchHeader]. The version-2 bytes the batch producer emits come from a patch of V1.Bytes (I18-R2), which is no encoder layout of its own. The deprecated duplicate decoder in morph-l2/node/types has no encoder in its package: three absences, (0, 249) elsewhere [V0.Bytes], (1, 257) [V1.Bytes], (2, 257) [GenesisBatchHeader].

New, narrowing O2's 'no v2 encoder' to the codec package: ops/l2-genesis's GenesisBatchHeader (morph-l2/morph-deployer/morph-chain-ops/genesis, batch.go:31-67) is a standalone version-2 encoder. Every layout it has is 257 bytes from its own make at batch.go:53 with cell 0 ["const", 2]; cells 1..24 ["const", 0] (PutUint64 of constant 0); 25..56 bytes 0..31 of a call of github.com/morph-l2/go-ethereum/crypto.Keccak256Hash; 57..88 bytes 0..31 of the package variable emptyBlobVersionedHash; 89..120 ["const", 0]; 121..152 bytes 0..31 of field Root of the parameter genesisHeader; 153..248 ["const", 0]; 249..256 bytes 0..7 of a call of (*math/big.Int).Uint64 on genesisHeader.Number. All its return paths return a nil error. Nothing in the repo records this encoder.

Block-context codec (D3, whose case-study state is none): morph-l2/common/batch.HeightFromBlockContextBytes is a decoder reading exactly [(0, 8, be_uint)], ok iff len == 60 on lengths 0, 7, 8, 9, 59, 60, 61. Both block-context encoders, BuildBlockContext (common/batch, batch_cache.go:1826) and (*WrappedBlock).BlockContextBytes (node/types, consensus_message.go:106, through the inlined Uint64ToBigEndianBytes / Uint16ToBigEndianBytes), have only 60-byte layouts: cells 0..7 the block number (bytes of header.Number.Uint64() / of wb.Number), 8..15 header.Time / wb.Timestamp, 48..55 the GasLimit field, 56..57 and 58..59 bytes of uint16(txsNum) and uint16(l1MsgNum); each has a layout on the path where its BaseFee field is nil, with cells 16..47 ["const", 0]. So the height decoder reads exactly the 8 bytes the encoders write for the block number.

The deprecated duplicate decoder in morph-l2/node/types decodes exactly like common/batch: for the 16 BatchHeaderBytes methods both packages define (validate, Bytes, Hash, Version and the 12 getters other than BlobCommitHash, which node/types lacks), the extracted paths are equal once the package path is replaced and spans are blanked.

The TxsPayloadV2 result shares backing with the spare capacity of blockContexts (O36's precondition). (*BatchData).TxsPayloadV2's result has exactly two backing cases. In place, under len(X) + len(Y) <= cap(X) with X = cks.blockContexts and Y = cks.txsPayload: backing ["of", X], offset 0, len len(X) + len(Y), cap cap(X). Grow: fresh at batch_data.go:119, cap ["unknown", "growth"]. TxsPayloadV2's only write is the in-place append writing [len(X), len(X) + len(Y)) of X's backing, and it stores nothing, so the view's tail is X's spare capacity, beyond the field's len; (*BatchData).Append's in-place append at batch_data.go:35 writes the same backing from len(X) and stores the result back into the field. A view held across Append is therefore overwritten (the M1 law L_own_txspayload, replayed on Go, shows the consequence; here it is the extracted precondition).

In common/batch/batch_data.go the in-place writes into parameter-rooted backings are exactly five appends: Append at :35 (blockContexts), :36 (txsPayload) and :39 (l1TxHashes, inside the loop), TxsPayloadV2 at :119 (blockContexts) and EstimateCompressedSizeWithNewPayload at :126 (txsPayload: a second method that writes a field's spare capacity without storing the field). DataHash, Encode, calculateHash and combinePayloads write only buffers they allocate.

O37 (value-receiver cache write is lost; case-study state none): morph_batch's lost writes are exactly the two stores b.EncodedBytes = batchBytes in BatchHeaderV0.Bytes (batch_header.go:228) and BatchHeaderV1.Bytes (:258), each into the method's own copy of its value receiver b, field path [EncodedBytes]. Prior record: whitepaper.md (§11.3 O37, Appendix A F12.3) states that the value-receiver header cache write is lost; predicted is the extractor's static lost-write inventory (exactly these two stores, nothing else in morph_batch), which nothing in the repo records.

O4 / F3 localized (case-study state none): morph-l2/common/batch.RetrieveBlobBytes (blob.go:45-54) has four bounds sites, exactly one open: the index data[i*32] in the error branch at blob.go:49, with witness {var i, min 3968, max 4095} (data has 4096 * 31 = 126976 bytes and i ranges over 0..4095 under the loop at :47); blob[i*32] at :48 and the two slices of the copy at :51 are safe. The fixed copy morph-l2/common/blob.RetrieveBlobBytes (payload.go:43-52) indexes the 131072-byte blob in its error message instead, and its four sites are all safe. Prior record: docs/build_plan/gap_map.json (O4) and whitepaper App. A F3 / §11.3 O4 state the open index from 3968 at common/batch/blob.go:45-54 and that the common/blob copy is defined; predicted is that the static extractor, reading no document, lists exactly these four sites per copy with exactly this status and witness range.

O4's consumer chain: the call edges include (*Derivation).Start -go-> Start$1 (derivation.go:200), Start$1 -> derivationBlock (:207), derivationBlock -> fetchRollupDataByTxHash (:380, :428, :456), fetchRollupDataByTxHash -> parseBatch (:599), parseBatch -> (*BatchInfo).ParseBatch (:715) and ParseBatch -> morph-l2/common/batch.RetrieveBlobBytes (batch_info.go:116, callee analyzed) inside the range loop over batch.Sidecar.Blobs (in_loops [batch_info.go:114]); ParseBatch does not call the fixed morph-l2/common/blob.RetrieveBlobBytes. So the derivation loop reaches the open site of I18-P11 with blob bytes from L1. Prior record: docs/build_plan/gap_map.json (O4) names the caller node/derivation/batch_info.go:116; the chain from (*Derivation).Start, the edge kinds and in_loops are not recorded.

TxsPayloadV2's consumers: it has exactly two call sites in the analyzed packages, (*BatchCache).handleBatchSealing (batch_cache.go:1581), where the result's only use is argument 0 of morph-l2/common/blob.CompressBatchBytes (not common/batch's own CompressBatchBytes), and (*Derivation).rebuildBlob (verify_local.go:186), where its uses are argument 0 of morph-l2/common/blob.CompressBatchBytes (:189) and len. Into that CompressBatchBytes the parameter's uses are len and argument 0 of morph-l2/common/codec/zstd.CompressBatchBytes, whose parameter's uses are len and argument 0 of the external github.com/morph-l2/morph-da-codec/bindings/codec/zstd.CompressMorphDABatch (the skeleton producer -> compressor -> external codec).

Loop bounds as fuel, exactly these loops in these functions (tests_m2/_i18.EXPECTED_LOOPS): (*BatchData).Append range over l1TxHashes (batch_data.go:38, fuel len(l1TxHashes), no exit); (*BatchData).DataHash i < int(cks.blockNum) (:74, fuel that limit); common/batch and common/blob MakeBlobCanonical i < 4096 (blob.go:33, payload.go:31, exits break) and RetrieveBlobBytes i < 4096 (blob.go:47, payload.go:45, exits return); both MakeBlobTxSidecar i < (len(blobBytes) + 126976 - 1) / 126976 (blob.go:89, payload.go:87, exits return); DecodeTxsFromBytes `for {}` (blob.go:120) unbounded, fuel null, exits return, with a loop_bound coverage debt; ParsingTxs range over transactions (batch_cache.go:1755, exits return); aggregateBlobHashes range over hashes (:1791, no exit); (*BatchInfo).ParseBatch range over batch.Sidecar.Blobs (batch_info.go:114) and i < int(blockCount) with blockCount a phi (:209), both exits return; (*Derivation).rebuildBlob n from batchInfo.firstBlockNumber while n <= batchInfo.lastBlockNumber (verify_local.go:159), fuel last - first + 1, exits return.

Recorded, not counted (reclassified from a prediction by the prereg review): whitepaper.md Appendix A F3 ('the Go blob-retrieval error path indexes out of bounds for non-canonical elements at index >= 3968'), §11.3 O4 and docs/build_plan/gap_map.json (O4: common/batch/blob.go:45-54 formats data[i*32] with len(data) = 4096*31; the common/blob copy is defined) already state this outcome. Observed on the real code: with the prereg Go instrument, on kzg blobs whose field element e has a non-zero high-order byte, the real common/batch RetrieveBlobBytes returns an error for e = 0 and 3967 and panics for e = 3968 (runtime error: index out of range [126976] with length 126976) and e = 4095 ([131040] with length 126976); the real common/blob RetrieveBlobBytes returns an error for all four.
